99965.q: What do bees make dark forest honey from?
99965.e: Aphids give off a sweet juice called honeydew. Bees collect it and make forest honey from it.
99965.m: Forest honey is made from honeydew.

99966.q: Which device does the beekeeper use to get the honey out of the combs?
99966.e: In the honey extractor the combs spin fast. This flings the honey out.
99966.m: The beekeeper spins the honey out of the combs.

99967.e: Honey consists mostly of sugar. That is why it tastes sweet.

99968.q: How many spots does the best-known ladybird in our country have?
99968.e: The seven-spot ladybird is very well known here. It has red wing cases with seven black spots.
99968.m: The best-known ladybird has seven spots.

99969.q: Do the spots show a ladybird's age?
99969.e: The number of spots depends on the species. It does not change with age.
99969.m: The spots show the species, not the age.

99970.q: What does a ladybird do when in danger?
a: It gives off a yellow juice
99970.e: The ladybird gives off a yellow, bitter juice from its legs. Enemies do not like the taste.
99970.m: In danger, the ladybird gives off a bitter juice.

99971.q: What does the ladybird larva eat?
99971.e: The larvae eat aphids too, and a great many of them. They look quite different from the beetles.

99972.q: How do ladybirds often spend the winter?
99972.e: In autumn, ladybirds look for sheltered places such as cracks or leaves. Often lots of them lie together.
99972.m: Ladybirds like spending the winter in groups.

99973.q: What do many people see the ladybird as?
a: as a sign of bad luck
99973.e: The ladybird is a popular lucky charm. In German it is even called the lucky beetle.
99973.m: The ladybird is seen as a lucky charm.

99974.e: The red colour warns birds: I don't taste good. That is why they rarely eat it.

99975.q: What shape are the cells of a honeycomb?
99975.e: The honeycomb cells have six corners. That way they fit next to each other without gaps.

99976.q: What is the opening that bees fly through into the hive called?
99976.e: The bees fly in and out through the entrance hole. Guard bees keep watch there.
99976.m: Bees fly into the hive through the entrance hole.

99977.q: What does the beekeeper use to calm the bees?
99977.e: Smoke makes the bees calmer. The beekeeper uses a smoker for this.
99977.m: The beekeeper calms the bees with smoke.

99978.q: What does the beekeeper wear for protection against stings?
99978.e: A beekeeper's veil protects the face and neck from bee stings.
99978.m: The beekeeper protects their face with a veil.

99979.q: How many queens normally live in a beehive?
99979.e: A bee colony normally has only one queen.
99979.m: A bee colony has one queen.

99980.q: How do bees keep warm in winter?
99980.e: In winter the bees huddle closely together. In this winter cluster they shiver their muscles and make warmth.
99980.m: In winter bees keep warm in a cluster.

99981.q: Roughly how many bees live in a strong bee colony in summer?
99981.e: In summer about 40,000 to 60,000 bees live in a strong colony.
99981.m: A strong bee colony has tens of thousands of bees in summer.

100072.q: What should you do a lot of when you have a fever?
100072.e: When you have a fever, you sweat and lose a lot of water. That is why it is important to drink a lot.
100072.m: If you have a fever, drink plenty.

100073.q: How does your forehead often feel when you have a fever?
100073.e: With a fever, your whole body is warmer than usual. That is why your forehead often feels hot.
100073.m: With a fever, your forehead often feels hot.

100074.q: What do you often feel when a fever is rising?
a: You have to laugh a lot.
100074.e: When a fever rises, the body wants to get warmer. That is why you feel cold and shiver; this is called the chills.
100074.m: When a fever rises, you often feel cold and shiver.

100075.q: What usually happens when a fever goes down again?
100075.e: When a fever goes down, the body gives off heat. You often sweat a lot.
100075.m: When a fever goes down, you often sweat.

100076.q: When should you take a child with a fever to the doctor?
100076.e: A fever on its own is often not serious. But if a child seems very ill, is not drinking, or a very young baby has a fever, you should see a doctor.
100076.m: If a child seems very ill, you go to the doctor.

100077.q: What can an adult give a child with a high fever to bring it down?
100077.e: Fever medicine lowers the fever, and you feel better. The right amount is written in the leaflet or the doctor tells you.
100077.m: Fever medicine can bring down a high fever.

100078.q: What do you measure a fever with?
100078.e: A thermometer measures how warm the body is. That way you know whether someone has a fever.
100078.m: You measure a fever with a thermometer.

100079.q: In which unit does a thermometer in Switzerland show your temperature?
100079.e: In Switzerland, temperatures are measured in degrees Celsius. The unit is named after the Swede Anders Celsius.
100079.m: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

100080.q: What does a digital thermometer often do when it has finished measuring?
100080.e: Digital thermometers beep when the measurement is finished. Then you can read the number.
100080.m: A digital thermometer beeps when it has finished.

100081.q: What does a digital thermometer need to work?
100081.e: A digital thermometer has a small display and a sensor. Both run on electricity from a small battery.
100081.m: A digital thermometer runs on a battery.

100082.q: Where can you quickly measure a child's temperature with a special thermometer?
100082.e: There are ear thermometers. You hold one in the ear for a moment, and after a few seconds it shows the temperature.
100082.m: An ear thermometer measures in the ear.

100083.q: What should you do after using a thermometer?
100083.e: Germs can stick to the thermometer. That is why you clean it after use, for example with soap and water or disinfectant.

100084.q: How do many forehead thermometers measure temperature?
100084.e: Many forehead thermometers measure the heat given off by the skin. You do not have to touch the forehead, or only briefly.
100084.m: A forehead thermometer measures the warmth of the skin.

100085.q: What do you often have when you have a cold?
100085.e: With a cold, your nose often runs or gets blocked. Sometimes you also have a cough and a sore throat.
100085.m: With a cold, you often have a runny nose.

100086.e: A cold is caused by viruses. There are lots of different cold viruses.

100087.q: In which season are colds especially common?
100087.e: In winter, people are more often together in warm rooms. Cold viruses can spread easily there.
100087.m: Lots of people catch colds in winter.

100088.q: Where is the best place to sneeze so that you do not infect anyone?
a: Into the crook of your elbow
100088.e: If you sneeze into the crook of your elbow, you spread fewer germs. Otherwise your hands would carry the viruses everywhere.
100088.m: Sneeze and cough into the crook of your elbow.

100089.q: What helps you to catch fewer illnesses?
100089.e: Viruses often stick to your hands. If you wash your hands regularly with soap, you catch fewer illnesses.
100089.m: Washing your hands protects against infection.

100090.q: Roughly how long does a cold last?
100090.e: A cold usually lasts about a week. After that you are healthy again.
100090.m: A cold usually lasts about a week.

100091.q: Where do you throw a used paper tissue?
100091.e: A used tissue contains lots of viruses. That is why you throw it straight in the bin.
100091.m: Used tissues go in the bin.

100092.q: Which word describes a nose that is completely closed up?
100092.e: With a cold, the skin inside your nose swells. Then your nose is blocked and you breathe through your mouth.
100092.m: With a cold, your nose is often blocked.

100093.q: What can help to clear a blocked nose?
100093.e: A saltwater nasal spray moistens the nose and loosens the mucus. Afterwards you can breathe better.
100093.m: Saltwater nasal spray makes your nose moist and clear.

100094.q: When does a sore throat hurt most?
100094.e: With a sore throat, your throat is inflamed. When you swallow, food rubs against it, so that is when it hurts most.
100094.m: You feel a sore throat mainly when swallowing.

100095.q: What is often red and swollen when you have a sore throat?
100095.e: The tonsils are at the back of the throat. When they are inflamed, they become red and swollen.
100095.m: With a sore throat, the tonsils are often red.

100096.q: What often feels good when you have a sore throat?
100096.e: Warm tea with honey soothes the throat. Spicy or hard food irritates it.
100096.m: Warm tea with honey is good for your throat.

100097.q: What can you suck when you have a sore throat?
100097.e: Throat sweets make you produce more spit. That keeps your throat moist and eases the scratchiness.
100097.m: Throat sweets can ease a scratchy throat.

100098.q: Where is a compress sometimes put when you have a sore throat?
100098.e: A throat compress is a cloth that you wrap around your neck. Many people find it soothing when they have a sore throat.
100098.m: A throat compress goes around the neck.

100099.q: What can happen to your voice when your throat is inflamed?
100099.e: When your throat is inflamed, your vocal cords can also be irritated. Then your voice sounds hoarse.
100099.m: With a sore throat, your voice often becomes hoarse.

100100.q: What do people often gargle with when they have a sore throat?
100100.e: You take a little salt water into your mouth and gargle with it. Then you spit it out again.
100100.m: Some people gargle with salt water for a sore throat.

100101.q: Who looks into your throat when you have a sore throat?
100101.e: The doctor looks into your throat with a light. That way they can see how inflamed your throat is.
100101.m: The doctor looks into your throat with a light.

100102.q: What do you often have with a tummy bug?
100102.e: With a tummy bug, the stomach and gut are inflamed. You often have diarrhoea and are sick.
100102.m: With a tummy bug, you often have diarrhoea.

100103.q: What is most important when you have a tummy bug?
100103.e: Being sick and having diarrhoea makes the body lose a lot of water. That is why you need to drink small sips often.
100103.m: With a tummy bug, you should drink a lot.

100104.q: Which body parts are ill when you have a tummy bug?
100104.e: A tummy bug is an inflammation of the stomach and gut. It has nothing to do with real flu.
100104.m: With a tummy bug, the stomach and gut are ill.

100105.q: Which food is easy on the stomach when you have a tummy bug?
100105.e: Rusks are dry and light. Greasy and sweet food, on the other hand, is hard on the tummy.
100105.m: With a tummy bug, you eat light things like rusks.

100106.q: Why must you wash your hands well after a tummy bug?
100106.e: The germs that cause a tummy bug spread very easily. Washing your hands protects the others in your family.
100106.m: A tummy bug is very contagious.

100107.e: A tummy bug comes from tiny germs that you cannot see. They easily spread from person to person.
100107.m: A tummy bug comes from tiny germs.

100108.q: What is the best way to drink when you have a tummy bug?
100108.e: A poorly stomach cannot cope well with large amounts. Small sips are more likely to stay down.
100108.m: With a tummy bug, you drink in small sips.

100109.q: How long does a tummy bug usually last?
100109.e: A tummy bug is usually over after a few days. After that, your tummy still needs a little care.
100109.m: A tummy bug usually only lasts a few days.

100110.q: Who should give a child medicine?
100110.e: Medicines can do harm if you take the wrong amount. That is why an adult always gives them.

100111.q: Where do you buy medicines in Switzerland?
100111.e: Medicines are sold at the chemist's (pharmacy). The pharmacist gives advice.
100111.m: You buy medicines at the chemist's.

100114.q: What does the doctor write so that you can get a certain medicine?
100114.e: Some medicines are only available with a prescription from the doctor. You take the prescription to the pharmacy.
100114.m: For some medicines you need a prescription.

100115.q: Which germs do antibiotics help against?
100115.e: Antibiotics kill bacteria or slow down their growth. They do not help against viruses, for example with a cold.

100116.q: In what form do medicines you swallow often come?
100116.e: Many medicines come as tablets, capsules or syrup. You swallow them with a little water.
100116.m: Many medicines are swallowed as tablets.

100117.q: What should you do if a medicine is past its expiry date?
a: Take it back to the pharmacy
100117.e: Out-of-date medicines may no longer work properly. In Switzerland, you can hand them in at the pharmacy.
100117.m: Old medicines go back to the pharmacy.

100118.q: What do you take cough syrup for?
100118.e: Cough syrup is a liquid medicine. It is meant to ease a cough.
100118.m: Cough syrup helps with a cough.

100119.q: What do you use to measure out cough syrup?
100119.e: Many cough syrups come with a measuring spoon or cup. That way you take exactly the right amount.
100119.m: You measure cough syrup with a measuring spoon.

100120.q: What form does cough syrup have?
100120.e: Syrup is thick and runny and often sweet. That is why it is easy to swallow.

100121.q: Which cough remedy is often made at home from onions and sugar?
100121.e: For onion syrup, you chop onions finely and add sugar or honey. It is an old home remedy for coughs.
100121.m: Onion syrup is an old home remedy for coughs.

100122.q: Which plant is often in cough syrup for children?
100122.e: Many children's cough syrups contain an extract from ivy leaves. It is meant to loosen mucus.

100123.q: What should you do with the measuring spoon after the cough syrup?
100123.e: Syrup is sticky, and germs stay on the spoon. That is why you wash the measuring spoon after every use.
100123.m: Wash the measuring spoon after use.

100124.q: Why must you not drink cough syrup like a sweet treat?
100124.e: Cough syrup often tastes sweet, but it is a medicine. Too much of it can be harmful.
100124.m: Cough syrup is a medicine, not a sweet.

100125.q: Which sweet ingredient is in many home remedies for coughs?
100125.e: Honey forms a film over the throat and soothes it. But babies under one year old must not have honey.
100125.m: Honey is a popular home remedy for coughs.

100126.e: With bed rest, you stay in bed and take it easy. That way the body can build up strength.
100126.m: With bed rest, you stay in bed and rest.

100127.q: Why does sleep help you get better?
100127.e: When you sleep, the body saves energy. It needs this energy to fight the illness.
100127.m: The body recovers while you sleep.

100128.q: What should you not do when you have a fever?
100128.e: Sport is too tiring for the body when you have a fever. Only when you are healthy again can you do sport again.
100128.m: No sport when you have a fever.

100129.q: What do you do often during bed rest so that fresh air gets into the room?
100129.e: Fresh air is good for people who are ill. You open the window for a short time and keep warmly covered.
100129.m: Air a sickroom briefly and often.

100130.q: What is a quiet activity during bed rest?
100130.e: During bed rest you should not tire yourself out. An audiobook or a book are quiet activities.
100130.m: During bed rest you only do quiet things.

100131.q: Where should an ill child with a fever stay?
100131.e: With a fever, you need rest. Also, you can infect others, so you stay at home.
100131.m: With a fever, you stay at home.

100132.q: What is best to have next to the bed during bed rest?
100132.e: People who are ill should drink a lot. A glass of water or tea next to the bed reminds them.
100132.m: Keep something to drink next to a sickbed.

100133.q: What do you do during bed rest if your pyjamas are wet from sweating?
a: Put a winter coat on over them
100133.e: Wet clothes cool the body down and are uncomfortable. That is why you put on dry pyjamas after sweating.
100133.m: After sweating, you put on dry clothes.

100134.q: Which tea do people often drink for tummy ache?
100134.e: Camomile tea soothes the tummy. It is one of the best-known home remedies.

100135.q: Which tea do people often drink for a sore throat?
100135.e: Sage has been used for sore throats for a long time. You drink it as tea or gargle with it.
100135.m: Sage tea is often drunk for a sore throat.

100136.q: Which tea tastes fresh and cooling?
100136.e: Peppermint contains menthol. That is why the tea feels fresh and cool in your mouth.

100137.q: What is herbal tea made from?
100137.e: For herbal tea, you use dried leaves or flowers from plants. You pour hot water over them.
100137.m: Herbal tea is made from dried plants.

100138.q: Which tea is often given to small children for wind?
100138.e: Fennel soothes the tummy and helps against wind. Fennel tea is mild, so it is also suitable for children.

100139.q: Which part of the camomile plant is used to make tea?
100139.e: For camomile tea, you use the dried flowers. They are white with yellow centres.
100139.m: Camomile tea is made from the flowers.

100140.q: What must you be careful about when drinking freshly made tea?
100140.e: Tea is made with boiling water. That is why you let it cool down a little before you drink it.
100140.m: Let fresh tea cool down a little.

100141.q: Which tea do people often drink when they have a cold and a fever?
100141.e: Lime blossom tea is an old home remedy for colds. It is drunk warm.
100141.m: Lime blossom tea is a home remedy for colds.

100142.q: Roughly how long do you let herbal tea brew?
100142.e: The herbs need a few minutes in the hot water. Then the tea releases its flavour and its active ingredients.
100142.m: Let herbal tea brew for a few minutes.

100143.q: What do you see on the skin with chickenpox?
100143.e: With chickenpox, lots of small red spots and blisters form on the skin. They are very itchy.

100144.q: Why should you not scratch chickenpox blisters open?
a: You will then never be ill again
100144.e: Scratched blisters can become infected. Afterwards small scars are sometimes left.

100145.q: How often do people usually get chickenpox?
100145.e: Anyone who has had chickenpox is usually protected afterwards. That is why you normally only get it once.
100145.m: You usually only get chickenpox once.

100146.e: Chickenpox viruses fly through the air when people breathe and talk. That is why they spread very easily.

100147.e: Chickenpox is a typical childhood illness. Most people get it as children.

100148.e: There is a vaccination against chickenpox. It protects you from getting ill.

100149.q: What can help against the itching with chickenpox?
100149.e: A cooling lotion from the pharmacy soothes itchy skin. Warmth and scratchy wool often make the itching worse.
100149.m: A cooling lotion eases the itching.

100150.q: What do chickenpox blisters form after a few days?
100150.e: The blisters dry up after a few days. Then a scab forms, which later falls off.
100150.m: Chickenpox blisters dry up into scabs.

100151.q: Where do you put a calf compress?
100151.e: The calf is the back of the lower leg. You wrap damp cloths around it.
100151.m: A calf compress goes around the lower legs.

100152.q: What does a calf compress help against?
100152.e: Calf compresses can bring a high fever down a little. The damp cloth absorbs heat from the body.
100152.m: Calf compresses can lower a fever.

100153.q: What should the water for a calf compress be like?
100153.e: For calf compresses, you use water that is a little cooler than the body. Ice-cold water would be too unpleasant.
100153.m: Use lukewarm to cool water for calf compresses.

100154.q: When should you not use calf compresses?
a: When you are lying in bed
100154.e: When your feet are cold or you are shivering, the body wants to keep its warmth. Then you should not cool it down even more.
100154.m: No calf compresses when your feet are cold.

100155.q: What do you need for a calf compress?
100155.e: You dip a cloth in water, wring it out and wrap it around the calf. A dry cloth goes on top.
100155.m: For a calf compress you need cloths and water.

100156.q: What do you put over the wet cloth of a calf compress?
100156.e: A dry cloth goes over the damp cloth. That keeps the bed dry, and you take the compress off again after a few minutes.
100156.m: A dry cloth goes over the wet cloth.

100157.q: What do you do with the cloth before you put it around the calf?
100157.e: The cloth should be damp but not dripping wet. That is why you wring it out well first.
100157.m: Wring out the wet cloth before wrapping it.

100158.q: What effect does a calf compress have on the body?
100158.e: The water in the cloth evaporates and takes heat from the skin with it. That cools the body down.
100158.m: A calf compress cools the body.

100159.q: Who looks after children who are ill?
100159.e: A children's doctor specialises in children and young people. They know a lot about childhood illnesses.
100159.m: The children's doctor looks after ill children.

100160.q: What does the children's doctor use to listen to your heart and lungs?
100160.e: A stethoscope has two earpieces and a round chest piece. With it, the doctor listens to your heart and breathing.
100160.m: The doctor listens to your heart and lungs with a stethoscope.

100161.q: What is the technical term for children's medicine?
100161.e: Children's medicine is called paediatrics. A children's doctor is therefore a paediatrician.

100162.q: What do you get at the children's doctor to protect you against illnesses?
100162.e: You get vaccinations at the children's doctor. They protect against dangerous illnesses.
100162.m: You get vaccinations at the children's doctor.

100163.q: Where does the children's doctor look with a small light when you have earache?
100163.e: The doctor has a small ear scope with a light. With it, they can see deep into the ear as far as the eardrum.
100163.m: The doctor looks into the ear with a small light.

100164.q: What is often measured at a check-up with the children's doctor?
100164.e: At check-ups, the children's doctor measures height and weight. That way they can see whether a child is growing well.
100164.m: The children's doctor measures how tall a child is.

100165.q: What do you usually do before going to the children's doctor?
100165.e: Usually you first phone the children's doctor. That way you get an appointment.
100165.m: First make an appointment with the children's doctor.

100166.q: What is the room where you have to wait at the doctor's called?
100166.e: Before you go into the treatment room, you wait in the waiting room. There are often books and toys there.
100166.m: At the doctor's, you wait in the waiting room.

100167.q: Where do you go if a child suddenly becomes very ill at night?
100167.e: At night, the children's doctor's surgery is usually closed. In an emergency, you go to hospital or call the emergency number 144.
100167.m: In an emergency at night, the hospital helps.

100168.q: At what temperature does water boil in a saucepan at the seaside?
100168.e: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Then big bubbles rise.
100168.m: At the seaside water boils at 100 degrees.

100169.q: What rises in the saucepan when the water boils?
100169.e: When it boils, water at the bottom turns into steam. The steam rises as bubbles.
100169.m: Boiling water makes bubbles of steam.

100170.q: In the mountains, does water boil at more or less than 100 degrees?
100170.e: In the mountains less air presses on the water. That is why it boils below 100 degrees, and pasta takes longer to cook.
100170.m: On a high mountain water boils below 100 degrees.

100171.q: Why do saucepans often have plastic handles?
a: They do not get as hot.
100171.e: Plastic conducts heat badly. So you can touch the handles without burning yourself so quickly.
100171.m: Plastic handles do not get as hot.

100172.q: What material are many saucepans made of?
100172.e: Many saucepans are made of metal, for example stainless steel. Metal conducts heat well to the food.

100173.q: What happens if you fill a saucepan too full of water and boil it?
100173.e: Boiling water bubbles upwards. If the pan is too full, it runs over the edge.
100173.m: A pan that is too full boils over.

100174.q: Why does the water at the top of the pan get warm too, even though only the bottom is hot?
a: The water at the top stays cold.
100174.e: At the bottom the water gets warm and rises. Cooler water sinks down, so everything warms up evenly.
100174.m: Warm water rises in the pan.

100175.q: What can you see above a pan of boiling water?
100175.e: The hot steam cools down in the air. Tiny water droplets form, which we see as a white cloud.
100175.m: Above boiling water you see a white cloud.

100176.q: Why do you put a lid on the pan when cooking?
100176.e: The lid keeps the heat in the pan. That is why the water gets hot faster and starts to boil sooner.
100176.m: With a lid, water boils faster.

100177.q: What do you save if you cook with a lid?
100177.e: With a lid, less heat is lost. That is why you need less energy to cook.
100177.m: Cooking with a lid saves energy.

100178.q: What collects on the inside of the lid?
100178.e: The steam meets the cooler lid. There it turns back into water and forms drops.
100178.m: On the lid, steam turns back into water.

100179.q: Why is a metal lid hot after cooking?
a: The hot steam has heated it.
It was kept in the fridge.
100179.e: The steam from the pan gives its heat to the lid. That is why you only hold it by the handle or with an oven glove.
100179.m: A metal lid gets hot from the steam.

100180.q: How should you lift a lid off a hot pan?
100180.e: There is hot steam under the lid. If you lift it away from your body, the steam does not rush into your face.
100180.m: Lift a lid away from your body.

100181.q: Why do some lids have a small hole?
a: So that light can get in
So that flies can get in
100181.e: Some steam can escape through the small hole. That way the lid rattles less and things do not boil over so easily.
100181.m: Steam escapes through the hole in the lid.

100182.q: What is a glass lid useful for?
a: You can see into the pan.
100182.e: You can see the food through glass without lifting the lid. That way the heat stays in the pan.
100182.m: You can look into the pan through a glass lid.

100183.q: What can you use to put out a fire in a frying pan with oil?
100183.e: A lid takes away the fire's air, and it goes out. Never pour water on burning oil: it turns to steam instantly and throws burning oil everywhere.
100183.m: Smother an oil fire with a lid, never with water.

100184.q: Where is the heating element in many kettles?
100184.e: The heating plate is at the bottom in the base. It passes its heat directly to the water.
100184.m: The heating element in a kettle is in the base.

100185.q: What does a kettle need to heat up?
100185.e: A kettle is plugged into a socket. The electricity makes the heating plate hot.

100186.q: What white layer builds up in a kettle over time?
100186.e: Tap water has lime dissolved in it. When it is heated, the lime settles as a white layer.
100186.m: Limescale builds up in a kettle.

100187.q: What can you use to remove limescale from a kettle?
100187.e: Vinegar is acidic and dissolves the limescale. Afterwards you rinse the kettle out well with water.

100188.q: Which is usually faster: boiling water in a kettle or in a pan on the cooker?
a: In a pan on the cooker
100188.e: In a kettle the heating element is right next to the water. So little heat is lost and the water boils quickly.
100188.m: Water boils quickly in a kettle.

100189.q: Why should you only fill the kettle with as much water as you need?
100189.e: Every litre of water takes energy to heat. If you only boil as much as you need, you save electricity.
100189.m: Boiling only as much water as you need saves electricity.

100190.q: Why does a kettle have a scale with lines on the outside?
a: To read how much water is in it
100190.e: The scale shows how much water is inside. That way you do not fill it too much or too little.
100190.m: You read the amount of water on the scale.

100191.q: Why must a kettle not be dipped into the sink?
100191.e: Water and electricity are dangerous together. That is why electrical appliances must never be dipped in water.
100191.m: Never dip electrical appliances in water.

100192.q: Why should you never switch a kettle on without water?
a: It would then need more water
It would never switch off again
100192.e: Without water, nothing takes up the heat from the heating plate. The appliance can overheat and break.
100192.m: Only switch a kettle on with water in it.

100193.q: What must you not put in the microwave?
100193.e: Metal can make sparks in the microwave. That is why you only put suitable dishes in it.
100193.m: Metal does not belong in the microwave.

100194.q: What does the microwave do to food?
100194.e: The microwave produces invisible rays. They go into the food and make it warm.

100195.q: What turns round in many microwaves?
100195.e: The turntable slowly turns the food. That way it gets warm evenly from all sides.
100195.m: The turntable makes sure food warms evenly.

100196.q: What mainly gets warm in the microwave?
100196.e: Microwaves mainly make water particles vibrate. That is why moist food heats up well.
100196.m: In the microwave it is mainly the water in the food that heats up.

100197.q: What should you do after heating something in the microwave?
100197.e: In the microwave, food often heats unevenly. Stirring spreads the heat.

100198.q: What must you not put in the microwave whole in its shell?
100198.e: Steam quickly builds up inside the egg and cannot escape. Then the egg can burst.
100198.m: An egg in its shell can burst in the microwave.

100199.q: What do you hear when the microwave has finished?
100199.e: Many microwaves have a timer. When the time is up, there is a signal.
100199.m: A microwave gives a signal when it has finished.

100200.q: Why does the microwave door have a mesh?
a: It makes the door look nicer.
It is a strainer for noodles.
100200.e: The fine metal mesh lets light through, but not microwaves. That way the rays stay inside the appliance.
100200.m: The mesh in the door keeps the microwaves inside.

100201.q: What are the invisible waves that warm food in the microwave called?
100201.e: The appliance is named after the microwaves it produces. You cannot see them.
100201.m: A microwave warms food with invisible microwaves.

100202.q: Roughly how cold is it in a freezer?
100202.e: A freezer cools down to about -18 degrees. That way food keeps for a long time.

100203.q: What do you call it when frozen food goes soft again?
100203.e: If you take frozen food out of the freezer, it gets warmer. The ice in it melts, and it defrosts.
100203.m: Frozen food defrosts in the warmth.

100204.q: What happens to a full glass bottle of water in the freezer?
100204.e: Water expands when it turns into ice. The ice needs more room and can break the bottle.

a: So that it goes mouldy faster
100205.e: In great cold, bacteria and mould can hardly grow. That is why food keeps for a long time in the freezer.
100205.m: Frozen food keeps for a long time.

100206.q: What builds up on the walls of the freezer over time?
100206.e: Moisture from the air freezes on the cold walls. This makes a layer of ice, which you defrost now and then.
100206.m: Ice builds up in a freezer over time.

100207.q: What should you do quickly after taking something out of the freezer?
100207.e: When the door is open, warm air flows in. Then the appliance has to use more electricity to get cold again.
100207.m: Close the freezer door again quickly.

100208.q: What must you not put in the freezer?
100208.e: Hot food warms up the freezer, and other things could start to thaw. Let it cool down first.
100208.m: Let warm food cool down before freezing it.

100209.q: What can happen if you touch an ice-cold ice lolly directly with your tongue?
a: Your tongue can stick to it.
100209.e: Very cold ice makes the spit on your tongue freeze instantly. Then your tongue sticks to it.
100209.m: Very cold ice can stick to your tongue.

100210.q: What gets hot on the cooker?
100210.e: The hotplate gets hot and passes the heat on to the pan. That is how the food is cooked.

100211.q: Why should you not touch a hotplate after cooking?
a: It stays hot for a long time.
100211.e: A hotplate stores heat. It stays hot for a while after being switched off.
100211.m: A hotplate stays hot after cooking.

100212.q: What do you need for an induction hob?
a: Pans with iron in the base
100212.e: An induction hob heats the base of the pan directly. This only works if the base contains iron.
100212.m: An induction hob needs magnetic pans.

100213.q: How can you test whether a pan works on induction?
100213.e: If a magnet sticks to the base of the pan, the pan works on an induction hob. If it does not stick, the pan will not get warm.
100213.m: A magnet shows whether a pan works on induction.

100214.q: What burns on a gas cooker?
100214.e: On a gas cooker, gas burns with a blue flame. The flame heats the pan.
100214.m: A gas cooker cooks with a flame.

100215.q: Which hotplate is best for a small pan?
100215.e: If the hotplate is bigger than the pan, heat is lost around it. With the right hotplate you save energy.
100215.m: The pan and the hotplate should be the same size.

100216.q: What is often built into a cooker under the hotplates?
100216.e: Many cookers have an oven built in underneath. You bake cakes or bread in it.
100216.m: There is often an oven under the hotplates.

100217.q: On many ceramic hobs, what does a glowing ‘H’ show?
100217.e: The ‘H’ is the residual heat indicator. It glows as long as the switched-off hotplate is still hot.
100217.m: An ‘H’ on the hob warns that a hotplate is hot.

100218.q: Which kernels are used to make popcorn?
100218.e: Popcorn is made from a special kind of maize called popping corn. Its kernels have a hard shell.

100219.q: Why does the maize kernel burst open?
a: The steam pushes the shell open.
100219.e: The steam inside the kernel has no room. At some point the pressure is so great that the hard shell bursts open.
100219.m: The steam in the kernel bursts the shell.

100220.q: Why do you put a lid on the pan when making popcorn?
100220.e: Bursting kernels jump up into the air. The lid stops them flying out of the pan.
100220.m: When making popcorn, put a lid on the pan.

100221.q: What colour is the inside of finished popcorn usually?
100221.e: The puffed-up inside of the maize kernel is white to light yellow. The brown shell stays on in small pieces.

100222.q: What is left if a maize kernel does not pop when you make popcorn?
100222.e: Some kernels have too little water or a damaged shell. They do not pop and stay hard.

100223.q: What do you often put in the pan before pouring in the maize kernels?
100223.e: The oil spreads the heat evenly around the kernels. That way they pop better and burn less.
100223.m: For popcorn you put a little oil in the pan.

100224.q: Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker?
100224.e: In the closed pressure cooker, the pressure rises. Then the water only boils at higher temperatures, and the food cooks faster.
100224.m: In a pressure cooker it gets hotter than 100 degrees.

100225.q: What is special about the lid of a pressure cooker?
a: It just rests loosely on top.
100225.e: The lid is locked firmly and has a rubber seal. That way the steam cannot simply escape.
100225.m: A pressure cooker is sealed tight.

100226.q: What do you often hear when steam escapes from the valve of a pressure cooker?
100226.e: When there is too much steam in the pan, the valve lets some of it out. The steam rushes through the narrow opening and hisses.

100227.q: When may you open a pressure cooker?
a: When there is no pressure left inside
100227.e: If the pan is still under pressure, hot steam can shoot out. That is why you only open it once the pressure has gone.
100227.m: Only open a pressure cooker when there is no pressure.

100228.q: What shows that there is pressure in a pressure cooker?
100228.e: There is a valve on the lid. It rises when there is pressure in the pan and often shows rings.
100228.m: The valve shows the pressure in a pressure cooker.

100229.q: What do you save with a pressure cooker?
100229.e: Because the food is cooked faster, the cooker has to be on for less time. That saves time and energy.
100229.m: A pressure cooker saves time and energy.

100230.q: What is often cooked in a pressure cooker because it otherwise takes a long time?
100230.e: Potatoes take about 20 minutes or more in a normal pan. In a pressure cooker they are soft much sooner.
100230.m: Potatoes get soft faster in a pressure cooker.

100231.q: Why does a pressure cooker always need some water?
a: Without water there is no steam.
100231.e: The pressure in the pan comes from steam. Without water no steam is made, and the pan can be damaged.
100231.m: A pressure cooker always needs some water.

100232.q: What do you make from cream with a whisk?
100232.e: With a whisk you beat liquid cream until it becomes stiff. Then it is called whipped cream.
100232.m: You make whipped cream with a whisk.

100233.q: What do you beat into the cream with a whisk?
100233.e: The wires of the whisk whirl air into the cream. Lots of tiny air bubbles make it fluffy.
100233.m: A whisk beats air into cream.

100234.q: What do you get if you beat egg white with a whisk for a long time?
100234.e: When it is beaten, the egg white traps lots of air bubbles. It turns white and firm and becomes stiff egg whites.
100234.m: Beaten egg white becomes stiff and white.

100236.q: What happens if you whip cream for far too long?
100236.e: If you whip it too long, the fat in the cream clumps together. That makes butter.
100236.m: Cream whipped too long turns into butter.

100237.q: What material are the wires of a whisk usually made of?
100237.e: The wires are usually made of stainless steel. They are bendy, do not rust and are easy to clean.
100237.m: The wires of a whisk are usually metal.

100238.q: What is faster than a whisk used by hand?
100238.e: An electric hand mixer turns its beaters very fast. That way the cream gets stiff more quickly.
100238.m: Whipping is faster with a mixer.

100239.q: What should cream be like so that it whips well?
100239.e: Cold cream gets stiff faster when it is whipped. Warm cream hardly firms up, and frozen cream cannot be whipped at all.
100239.m: Cream whips best when well chilled.

100240.q: What do you need a pot holder for?
100240.e: A pot holder protects your hands from hot handles. That way you do not burn yourself.
100240.m: Use a pot holder to hold hot pans.

100241.q: Why does a thick pot holder protect well against heat?
a: It is as cold as ice.
100241.e: Fabric with lots of tiny air pockets only lets heat through slowly. That is why your hand hardly feels the heat.
100241.m: A thick pot holder hardly lets heat through.

100242.q: Why should a pot holder be dry?
a: A wet one conducts heat faster.
100242.e: Water conducts heat much better than dry fabric. You can burn yourself with a wet pot holder.
100242.m: A pot holder must be dry.

100243.q: What is a glove for taking hot trays out of the oven called?
100243.e: An oven glove is like a pot holder but protects your whole hand. You use it to take hot trays out of the oven.
100243.m: Use an oven glove to take hot trays out of the oven.

100244.q: What are pot holders often made of?
100244.e: Cotton is thick and soft and does not melt like some plastics. That is why many pot holders are made of cotton.
100244.m: Many pot holders are made of cotton.

100245.q: What is a small loop on a pot holder for?
100245.e: You use the loop to hang the pot holder on a hook. That way it is always to hand.
100245.m: You hang up a pot holder by its loop.

100246.q: What can you put a hot pan on so that the table is not damaged?
100246.e: A trivet protects the table from the heat. Without it, marks or burns could appear.
100246.m: Put hot pans on a trivet.

100247.q: Why should you never hold a pot holder close to an open flame?
100247.e: A pot holder is made of fabric and can burn. That is why you keep it away from flames.
100247.m: A pot holder can catch fire.

100248.q: What happens to ice cubes in a glass of water?
100248.e: Ice is lighter than the same amount of water. That is why ice cubes float on the surface.

100249.q: What can you put in the ice cube tray before freezing to make the ice cubes look pretty?
100249.e: If you put berries or mint leaves in the water, they freeze into the ice. That makes the ice cubes look lovely in a drink.
100249.m: Berries in ice cubes look pretty.

100250.q: What is it called when ice turns into water?
100250.e: When ice gets warm, it melts. Solid ice turns into liquid water.

100251.q: Why does a drink with ice cubes get cold?
a: The ice gives off cold like a cooker.
100251.e: Ice needs heat to melt. It takes this heat from the drink, so the drink gets cooler.
100251.m: Ice cubes take heat away from a drink.

100252.q: Where does an ice cube melt faster?
100252.e: Warm water gives a lot of heat to the ice. That is why it melts quickly there.
100252.m: Ice melts quickly in warm water.

100253.q: What can you see on the outside of a cold glass with ice cubes?
100253.e: The air contains water vapour. On the cold glass it turns back into water and forms drops.
100253.m: Drops form on the outside of a cold glass.

100254.q: What happens to the water level when ice cubes melt in the glass?
100254.e: A floating ice cube pushes aside as much water as it weighs. That is why the glass does not overflow when it melts.
100254.m: Melting ice cubes do not make a glass overflow.

100255.q: What shape is an ice cube usually?
100255.e: You pour water into a tray with small compartments and freeze it. The compartments are often cube-shaped.
100255.m: Ice cubes are usually shaped like a cube.

100256.q: What does a toaster do to bread?
a: It makes it brown and crispy.
It makes it soft and wet.
100256.e: In the toaster, the bread is heated from both sides. It turns brown and crispy.

100257.q: What glows red in a toaster?
100257.e: Electricity flows through thin wires and makes them very hot. They glow red and toast the bread.
100257.m: Heating wires glow in a toaster.

100258.q: What must you never put into a toaster that is switched on?
100258.e: Metal conducts electricity. If you reach into the toaster with a fork, you can get a dangerous electric shock.
100258.m: Never put metal into a toaster.

100259.q: What happens when the bread in the toaster is ready?
100259.e: In many toasters a spring pushes the bread up when the time is up. Then you can take it out.

100260.q: What happens if you toast bread for too long?
100260.e: With too much heat the bread burns. It turns black and tastes bitter.
100260.m: Bread toasted for too long burns.

100261.q: What do you set with the dial on a toaster?
100261.e: With the dial you set how long it toasts for. A longer time makes the bread darker.
100261.m: On a toaster you set how brown the bread gets.

100262.q: What collects at the bottom of the toaster?
100262.e: Small crumbs fall down while toasting. Empty the crumb tray now and then, when the toaster is off and cold.

100263.q: What do you put on top of some toasters to warm up bread rolls?
100263.e: Some toasters have a wire rack that fits on top. You put rolls on it, and the heat from below warms them up.
100263.m: With a bun warmer rack a toaster warms up rolls too.

100661.q: In which kind of area do especially many cacti grow?
a: In the ice at the North Pole
100661.e: Cacti are adapted to great drought. That is why many of them are found in deserts and semi-deserts.

100662.q: What are a cactus's spines for?
100662.e: The sharp spines stop thirsty animals from nibbling the cactus. They also give a little shade.
100662.m: Spines protect the cactus from hungry animals.

100663.q: What does the giant saguaro cactus in the desert look like?
a: Like a star on the ground
100663.e: The saguaro can grow over 12 metres tall. With its arms it looks like a big candlestick.
100663.m: The saguaro is a giant among cacti.

100664.q: What do many cacti show only for a short time?
100664.e: Many cacti produce splendid, colourful flowers. Some flowers last only a single day or night.
100664.m: Even a spiny cactus can flower beautifully.

100665.q: How often does a cactus on the windowsill need water?
100665.e: A cactus stores water and cannot cope with waterlogging. Too much watering makes its roots rot.
100665.m: A cactus is watered only rarely.

100666.q: Why must you peel the fruit of the prickly pear carefully?
100666.e: The prickly pear cactus produces sweet fruits. Their skin has fine spines, so they are peeled carefully.

100667.q: Where do the leaves grow on a palm tree?
100667.e: Most palms have a trunk without branches. The big leaves form a tuft at the top.
100667.m: Palms wear their leaves like a hat on top.

100668.q: Which sweet fruits grow on palms in the desert?
100668.e: The date palm grows in desert oases. Its sweet fruits are dates.
100668.m: Dates grow on the date palm.

100669.q: In which Swiss canton do you see especially many palms outdoors?
100669.e: The climate in Ticino is mild. There, for example, windmill palms even grow wild in the woods.

100670.q: Which hard fruit with juice inside grows on a palm?
100670.e: The coconut grows on the coconut palm. Inside it has white flesh and coconut water.
100670.m: The coconut grows on the coconut palm.

100671.q: What weather do most palms like?
100671.e: Most palms grow in the tropics and subtropics. Only a few kinds can cope with frost.

100672.q: From the stems of which plants is rattan furniture made?
100672.e: Rattan comes from climbing palms in Asia. Their long, flexible stems are woven into chairs and baskets.

100673.q: How tall can some palms grow?
a: Only as tall as a child
Only as tall as a table
Only as tall as a blade of grass
100673.e: The tallest palm is the wax palm in Colombia. It can grow about 60 metres tall, as tall as a tower block.

100674.q: What is a bamboo cane usually like inside?
100674.e: A bamboo cane is usually hollow. It is divided into sections by joints.

100675.q: What is often made from bamboo in Asia?
100675.e: Bamboo is light, hard and grows back quickly. It is used to make chopsticks and baskets, for example.
100675.m: Many useful things are made from bamboo.

100676.q: Which part of bamboo can you eat cooked?
100676.e: Young bamboo shoots are popular in Asian cooking. They must be cooked before you eat them.
100676.m: Bamboo shoots are eaten only cooked.

100677.q: On which continent do especially many kinds of bamboo grow?
100677.e: Most kinds of bamboo grow in Asia, for example in China. Some kinds also grow in America and Africa.
100677.m: Asia is the continent of bamboo forests.

100678.q: How often do many kinds of bamboo flower?
100678.e: Many kinds of bamboo flower only very rarely, sometimes only after decades. Often all the plants of one kind then flower at the same time.
100678.m: Bamboo flowering is a rare event.

100679.q: On which continent does the African baobab grow?
100679.e: The African baobab grows in the savannahs of Africa south of the Sahara.
100679.m: The baobab is a tree of the African savannah.

100680.q: What is another name for the monkey bread tree?
100680.e: The monkey bread tree is also called the baobab. It is known by this name in many countries.
100680.m: The monkey bread tree and the baobab are the same tree.

100681.q: What does the baobab store in its thick trunk?
100681.e: The mighty trunk can store a great deal of water. That way the tree survives long dry seasons.
100681.m: The thick baobab trunk is a water store.

100682.q: Why do people say the baobab stands on its head?
a: Its bare branches look like roots
Its roots are up in the sky
It has no trunk at all
100682.e: Without leaves, the short, thick branches look like roots. That is why the tree looks as if it were standing on its head.
100682.m: The bare baobab looks like an upside-down tree.

100683.e: Baobabs are among the longest-living trees. Some are well over 1,000 years old.
100683.m: A baobab can live for over a thousand years.

100684.q: Where does the monkey bread tree get its name from?
100684.e: The tree's big fruits are called monkey bread. Baboons and other animals like eating them.
100684.m: Monkeys like nibbling the fruit of the monkey bread tree.

100685.q: When does the baobab lose its leaves?
100685.e: In the long dry season the tree sheds its leaves. That way it loses less water.
100685.m: Without leaves the baobab saves water.

100686.q: In which book does a character pull up young baobabs on his planet?
100686.e: In the book “The Little Prince” by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, the little prince has to pull up young baobabs. Otherwise they would burst his tiny planet.
100686.m: The little prince fights against baobabs.

100687.q: Although it looks like a tree, what is the banana plant really?
100687.e: The banana plant has no wooden trunk. Its false stem is made of tightly rolled leaves, so it counts as a herbaceous plant.
100687.m: The banana plant is not a real tree.

100688.q: Which way do bananas bend as they grow?
100688.e: Young bananas first hang downwards. Then they grow upwards towards the light and so become curved.
100688.m: Bananas are curved because they grow towards the light.

100689.e: Bananas are harvested green. Only as they ripen do they turn yellow and sweet.

100690.q: Which country sells the most bananas to other countries?
100690.e: Ecuador in South America is the biggest exporter of bananas. Many bananas in Swiss shops come from South America.

100691.q: What is no longer found in the bananas we eat?
100691.e: Wild bananas have lots of hard seeds. The bananas bred for eating only have tiny dark dots left.
100691.m: Eating bananas no longer have hard seeds.

100692.q: What happens to the banana stem after the harvest?
a: It dies and new shoots grow
100692.e: Each false stem bears fruit only once. After that it dies and new shoots grow from the ground.
100692.m: A banana stem bears fruit only once.

100693.q: Can you eat a plantain raw like a normal banana?
a: No, you cook or fry it first
Yes, but only with the skin
No, you only drink its juice
100693.e: Plantains are big and starchy. Raw they hardly taste of anything, so they are boiled or fried like potatoes.

100694.q: Which plant does the coconut grow on?
100694.e: Coconuts grow in bunches at the top of the coconut palm. This palm grows on tropical coasts.
100694.m: The coconut grows on the coconut palm.

100695.q: What is the clear liquid in a young coconut called?
100695.e: Young coconuts are filled with coconut water. It is clear and tastes slightly sweet.
100695.m: There is coconut water in a young coconut.

100696.q: How do coconuts get across the sea to other islands?
100696.e: The coconut has a thick, airy layer of fibres. That is why it floats and can drift across the sea to new beaches.
100696.m: Coconuts can float across the sea.

100697.q: What is the coconut really, to plant scientists?
100697.e: Botanically, the coconut is not a nut. Like the cherry or plum, it is a stone fruit with a hard stone.
100697.m: The coconut is a stone fruit.

100698.q: What is made from the fibres of the coconut?
100698.e: The tough fibres around the coconut are called coir. They are used to make doormats, ropes and brushes.
100698.m: Doormats are made from coconut fibres.

100699.q: How many dark “eyes” does a coconut have?
100699.e: At one end the coconut has three dark spots. The young shoot later grows out through one of them.

a: By pressing the flesh with water
By boiling coconut water for a long time
100700.e: For coconut milk, the grated flesh is mixed with water and pressed. It is not real milk.
100700.m: Coconut milk comes from the flesh.

100701.q: What does the Venus flytrap catch?
100701.e: The Venus flytrap catches mainly insects and spiders with its leaves. It then digests them.

100702.q: Which group of plants does the Venus flytrap belong to?
100702.e: The Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant. It gets nutrients from the animals it catches.
100702.m: The Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant.

100703.q: How does the Venus flytrap catch its prey?
100703.e: The trap leaves are built like two halves. If an insect touches them, they snap shut in a flash.
100703.m: The Venus flytrap's trap snaps shut.

100704.q: How many times does an insect usually have to touch the trigger hairs before the trap snaps shut?
100704.e: There are fine trigger hairs inside the trap. It usually only closes when they are touched twice in quick succession.
100704.m: Two touches set off the trap.

100705.q: In which country does the Venus flytrap grow wild?
100705.e: The Venus flytrap grows wild only in a small area in North Carolina and South Carolina in the USA.
100705.m: The Venus flytrap comes from the USA.

100706.q: Why does the Venus flytrap catch insects?
100706.e: The plant grows in wet bogs that are poor in nutrients. The insects give it important nutrients such as nitrogen.
100706.m: Insects are fertiliser for the Venus flytrap.

100707.q: How fast does the Venus flytrap's trap close?
a: In a fraction of a second
100707.e: The trap closes in less than a second. That is one of the fastest movements in the plant kingdom.
100707.m: The Venus flytrap snaps shut in a flash.

100708.q: What do the edges of the trap leaves have so that the prey cannot escape?
100708.e: There are long bristles on the edge of the trap leaves. When the trap is shut, they interlock like bars.

100709.q: Roughly how long does a trap stay closed for digestion?
100709.e: After a catch, the trap stays closed for several days. During this time the plant digests the prey.
100709.m: The Venus flytrap digests its prey for days.

100710.q: Where do many orchids grow in the rainforest?
100710.e: Many tropical orchids are epiphytes. They grow on trees to be closer to the light.
100710.m: Many orchids sit high up on trees.

100711.q: Which spice comes from an orchid?
100711.e: Vanilla is obtained from the pods of a climbing orchid. It originally comes from Mexico.

100712.q: Roughly how many kinds of orchid are there?
100712.e: Orchids form one of the largest plant families in the world. About 28,000 kinds are known.
100712.m: There are a huge number of orchid kinds.

100713.q: What is a rare wild orchid in Switzerland with a yellow, shoe-shaped flower called?
100713.e: The lady's slipper has a yellow flower that looks like a little shoe. It is protected in Switzerland.
100713.m: The lady's slipper is a Swiss orchid.

100714.e: Orchid seeds are as small as specks of dust. The wind can carry them far.
100714.m: Orchid seeds are as fine as dust.

100715.q: What do many potted orchids have that sticks out of the pot?
100715.e: Many indoor orchids come from epiphytes. With their aerial roots they take up water from the air.

100716.q: How does the Ophrys orchid attract insects?
a: Its flower looks like a female insect
It offers especially a lot of nectar
It catches insects with sticky hairs
100716.e: The flower of the Ophrys looks like a female insect and smells similar. Males fly to it and pollinate it as they do. It offers no nectar.
100716.m: The Ophrys orchid tricks insects with its flower.

100717.q: What is often made from cotton?
100717.e: Fabrics are made from cotton fibres. Many T-shirts, socks and bed sheets are made of it.
100717.m: Many clothes are made of cotton.

100718.q: Where are the white fibres of the cotton plant?
100718.e: After flowering, the plant forms seed pods called bolls. When they burst open, the white fibres on the seeds spill out.
100718.m: Cotton spills out of the bolls.

100719.e: Cotton needs a lot of warmth and sun. It is grown in warm countries.

100720.q: Which country is one of the biggest cotton producers in the world?
100720.e: India and China are among the countries that grow the most cotton. No cotton grows in fields in Switzerland.
100720.m: India grows a great deal of cotton.

100721.q: What does cotton need a great deal of when it is grown?
100721.e: Growing cotton takes a lot of water. The fields often have to be irrigated.

100722.q: What is made from cotton fibres before fabric is woven?
100722.e: The fibres are cleaned and spun into thread. Fabrics are woven or knitted from this yarn.
100722.m: Yarn is spun from cotton fibres.

100723.q: What material are most jeans made of?
100723.e: Jeans are sewn from denim. That is a sturdy fabric made of cotton.
100723.m: Jeans are mostly made of cotton.

100724.e: Chocolate is made from the beans of the cocoa tree. Usually sugar and often milk are added.
100724.m: Without cocoa beans there is no chocolate.

100725.q: Where do the fruits of the cocoa tree grow?
a: Only on the tips of the leaves
100725.e: The flowers and fruits of the cocoa tree grow right on the trunk and the thick branches. That looks unusual.
100725.m: Cocoa pods hang right on the trunk.

100726.q: On which continent is the most cocoa harvested?
100726.e: Most cocoa beans come from West Africa, for example from Ivory Coast and Ghana.
100726.m: A lot of cocoa comes from Africa.

100727.q: Where does the cocoa tree originally come from?
100727.e: The cocoa tree comes from the tropical forests of Central and South America. Later it was taken to Africa and Asia.
100727.m: The cocoa tree comes from America.

100728.q: Where does the cocoa tree grow best?
100728.e: The cocoa tree needs warmth, lots of rain and shade. That is why it grows in tropical rainforest.

100729.q: What is done first with cocoa beans after the harvest?
100729.e: The beans are left to ferment with the fruit pulp for a few days and then dried. Only this creates the cocoa flavour.
100729.m: Cocoa beans must ferment and dry.

100730.q: What else did the Aztecs use cocoa beans for?
100730.e: Among the Aztecs, cocoa beans were very valuable. You could pay with them.
100730.m: Cocoa beans were money for the Aztecs.

100731.q: Where does Switzerland get its cocoa beans from?
100731.e: The cocoa tree needs a tropical climate and does not grow outdoors in Switzerland. The beans for Swiss chocolate are imported.
100731.m: Swiss chocolate needs cocoa from the tropics.

100732.q: Which part of the cocoa bean does white chocolate contain?
100732.e: White chocolate contains cocoa butter, which is the fat of the bean. The brown cocoa powder is missing from it.
100732.m: White chocolate is made of cocoa butter.

100733.q: Where does the pineapple originally come from?
100733.e: The pineapple comes from South America. Christopher Columbus came across it on his voyages.
100733.m: The pineapple comes from South America.

100734.q: What can you do with the crown of leaves of a pineapple?
a: Plant it for a new plant
100734.e: The crown of leaves can grow roots. If you plant it, a new pineapple plant grows.
100734.m: A new plant grows from the pineapple crown.

100735.q: Roughly how long does it take for a pineapple plant to bear fruit?
100735.e: A pineapple plant needs more than a year until the fruit is ripe. Each plant usually forms only one big fruit at a time.

100736.q: What is a pineapple really made of?
100736.e: The pineapple is a multiple fruit. Many small flowers become berries that grow together into one fruit.
100736.m: A pineapple is made of many berries grown together.

100737.q: What can fresh pineapple do on your tongue?
a: It makes your tongue as cold as ice
It numbs your tongue like at the dentist's
100737.e: Fresh pineapple contains a substance that irritates the tongue. That is why it sometimes tingles or stings a little.
100737.m: Fresh pineapple can tingle on your tongue.

100739.q: Which group of islands used to be famous for huge pineapple fields?
100739.e: In the 20th century there were huge pineapple plantations in Hawaii. Today most pineapples are grown in other countries.
100739.m: Hawaii was once a pineapple paradise.

100740.q: Which country has the mango as its national fruit?
100740.e: The mango is the national fruit of India. It has been grown there for thousands of years.

100741.q: What is in the middle of a mango?
100741.e: The mango is a stone fruit. In its middle there is a big, flat stone.
100741.m: The mango has a big stone.

100742.q: How tall can a mango tree grow?
100742.e: Mango trees can grow very big and reach over 30 metres. On plantations they are usually kept smaller.
100742.m: A mango tree can grow very tall.

100743.q: What colour is the flesh of a ripe mango usually?
100743.e: Ripe mangoes have juicy, yellow to orange flesh. The skin can be green, yellow or red.
100743.m: Mango flesh is yellow to orange.

100744.q: Where do mango trees grow outdoors?
a: In cold countries in the north
100744.e: Mango trees need a lot of warmth. They grow in warm countries such as India, Thailand or Brazil.
100744.m: Mango trees grow in warm countries.

100745.q: The mango tree is evergreen. What does that mean?
a: It has leaves all year round
100745.e: An evergreen tree never sheds all its leaves at once. The mango tree has green leaves all year round.
100745.m: Evergreen trees are green all year round.

100746.q: What is an Indian yoghurt drink, often made with mango, called?
100746.e: Lassi is a drink made from yoghurt that is popular in India. Mango lassi is a well-known kind.
100746.m: Mango lassi is an Indian drink.

100747.q: How old can mango trees get?
100747.e: Mango trees live a long time. Some still bear fruit after more than 100 years.
100747.m: Mango trees live to a great age.

100748.q: Where is a golden barrel cactus usually kept in our country?
100748.e: The golden barrel cactus comes from Mexico and is round as a ball with golden yellow spines. Here it is a popular house plant.
100748.m: The golden barrel cactus is a popular house plant.

100749.q: How do the flat, widely spreading roots help the cactus?
a: They soak up water quickly after rain
They look for groundwater deep down
100749.e: Many cacti have roots just under the ground that spread out far. After a short shower they quickly take up a lot of water.
100749.m: The cactus's roots drink quickly after rain.

100750.q: What is the stem of bamboo called?
100750.e: Bamboo is a grass. As in other grasses, its stem is called a culm. It is divided by joints.
100750.m: The stem of bamboo is called a culm.

100751.q: Which animal eats almost nothing but bamboo?
100751.e: The giant panda lives in the mountain forests of China. Almost all its food is bamboo, and it eats many kilograms of it a day.
100751.m: The giant panda eats almost nothing but bamboo.

100752.q: How tall can the biggest kinds of bamboo grow?
100752.e: Giant bamboo from Asia can grow over 20 metres tall. That is as tall as a building with many storeys.
100752.m: Giant bamboo grows as tall as a building.

100753.q: What is the best way to water an indoor orchid?
a: Fairly rarely and with no standing water in the pot
Fill the pot to the brim every day
100753.e: In the wild, indoor orchids grow on trees. Their roots cannot cope with waterlogging and otherwise rot. That is why they are watered sparingly.
100753.m: Orchids don't like standing water in the pot.

100754.q: Which animals visit the flowers of the baobab at night?
100754.e: The big white flowers open in the evening. Fruit bats visit them at night and carry the pollen on.

100851.q: Who comes when you call 144 in Switzerland?
100851.e: The number 144 is the emergency number for the ambulance service. It sends an ambulance with paramedics.
100851.m: When you call 144, the ambulance comes.

100852.q: How much does a call to the emergency number 144 cost?
100852.e: Emergency calls in Switzerland are free. That way everyone can get help straight away.

100853.q: What is especially important to say when you call 144?
100853.e: The rescue team must know where to go. That is why you say exactly where you are.
100853.m: When I make an emergency call, I say exactly where I am.

100855.q: Which number do you dial in Switzerland if there is a fire?
100855.e: 118 is the number for the fire brigade. It comes to every fire.
100855.m: If there is a fire, I call the fire brigade on 118.

100856.q: What is the number for the police in Switzerland?
100856.e: You can reach the police on 117. They help, for example, after a burglary.

100857.q: Which number do you call if a child has swallowed something poisonous?
100857.e: 145 is the number of Tox Info Suisse. Experts there help with poisoning around the clock; if someone is unconscious, you dial 144.

100858.q: Are you allowed to call 144 for fun?
100858.e: Anyone who calls for fun blocks the line. Then someone in a real emergency might not get through.
100858.m: I only call the emergency number in an emergency.

100859.q: What kind of help is the number 144 for?
100859.e: 144 is for people who need medical help quickly, for example after an accident.

100860.q: Which emergency number works all over Europe?
100860.e: 112 is the European emergency number. It works in all EU countries and in Switzerland too.

100861.q: Does the number 112 also work in Switzerland?
100861.e: 112 also works in Switzerland. You can get help quickly with it too.

100862.q: When is the number 112 especially useful?
100862.e: Abroad, you often do not know the emergency numbers. 112 is the same in many European countries.
100862.m: On holiday in Europe, I dial 112 in an emergency.

100863.q: How many digits does the European emergency number have?
100863.e: The European emergency number is 112, so one, one, two. That is three digits.
100863.m: The European emergency number has only three digits.

100864.q: Which emergency number is used mainly in the USA?
100864.e: In the USA and Canada, people dial 911. In Europe, it is 112.
100864.m: In Europe I dial 112, and in the USA 911.

100865.q: Who do you reach in Switzerland when you dial 112?
100865.e: If you dial 112, you get through to an emergency control centre. They send the right help.
100865.m: With 112, I reach an emergency control centre.

100866.q: What can you dial the European emergency number 112 for?
100866.e: On 112, they help you with accidents, fire or danger. It does not matter what kind of emergency it is.

100867.q: Can you call 112 with a mobile phone too?
100867.e: 112 works with mobiles and landlines. That is why you can also dial it when you are out and about.
100867.m: I can dial 112 on a mobile phone too.

100868.q: What do you do first with a small graze?
a: Not look at it at all
100868.e: First you wash dirt out of the wound with clean water. Then a plaster goes on.

100869.q: Which part of a plaster should you not touch with your fingers?
a: The soft pad in the middle
The sticky strips on the outside
100869.e: The pad lies directly on the wound. It should stay clean so that no germs get in.
100869.m: I do not touch the pad of a plaster.

100870.q: What is a plaster on a small wound for?
100870.e: The plaster covers the wound. That way less dirt and fewer germs get in.
100870.m: A plaster protects a wound from dirt.

100871.q: Where should plasters be kept at home?
100871.e: In the first aid kit, everything for first aid is in one place. That way you can find it quickly.
100871.m: I keep plasters in the first aid kit.

100872.q: When do you put a new plaster on a wound?
a: When the old one is wet or dirty
When the old one is still completely clean
100872.e: A wet or dirty plaster no longer protects well. Then you put on a new clean plaster.
100872.m: I replace a dirty plaster with a new one.

100873.q: When is a plaster NOT enough any more?
a: When a wound is bleeding heavily
100873.e: For heavy bleeding, you need a bandage and help from adults. A plaster is only for small wounds.
100873.m: If there is heavy bleeding, I get help straight away.

100874.q: What do you do before you put a plaster on someone?
100874.e: Clean hands carry fewer germs to the wound. That is why you wash them first.
100874.m: Before treating a wound, I wash my hands.

100875.q: What can you use to treat a clean wound against germs before putting on a plaster?
100875.e: A disinfectant from the first aid kit kills germs. Then you put the plaster on.
100875.m: Disinfectant kills germs in a wound.

100876.q: What is the wound called when you fall on your knee and scrape the skin?
100876.e: With a graze, the top layer of skin has been rubbed off. It usually only bleeds a little.
100876.m: Scraped skin is called a graze.

100877.q: What is a roll of bandage usually made of?
100877.e: A bandage is made of fabric such as gauze or stretchy material. You can wrap it around a wound.
100877.m: A bandage is made of soft fabric.

100878.q: How tight should a bandage be?
100878.e: A bandage that is too tight cuts off the blood. A bandage that is too loose slips off.
100878.m: A bandage sits firmly, but not too tightly.

100879.q: How can you tell that a bandage on an arm is too tight?
a: The fingers turn blue and cold
The fingers turn warm and pink
100879.e: If too little blood reaches the fingers, they turn blue, cold or tingle. Then the bandage must be loosened.
100879.m: Blue, cold fingers show that a bandage is too tight.

100880.q: What is the cloth called that you can use to support an injured arm?
100880.e: With a triangular bandage, you can make an arm sling. That keeps the injured arm still.
100880.m: I support an arm with a triangular bandage.

100881.q: What do you do first if a wound is bleeding heavily?
a: Press firmly on the wound and get help
Rinse the wound with water and wait
Let the wound dry in the air
Stick a small plaster next to it
100881.e: Pressure on the wound slows the bleeding. At the same time, you get help or call the emergency number 144.
100881.m: With heavy bleeding, press firmly on the wound.

100882.q: Where in Switzerland can you often find a first aid kit?
100882.e: Many cars, schools and sports halls have a first aid kit. It contains bandages and plasters.
100882.m: Schools and cars have first aid kits.

100883.q: Why do you need disposable gloves when putting on a bandage?
a: To protect against blood and germs
100883.e: Gloves protect both helpers and injured people from germs. You find them in the first aid kit.
100883.m: I put on gloves when bandaging.

100884.q: What do you put directly on a wound first, before wrapping it?
100884.e: A sterile dressing lies cleanly on the wound. You wrap the bandage over it.
100884.m: A clean dressing goes on the wound first.

100885.q: What helps straight after spraining your foot?
100885.e: Cooling and raising it make the swelling less bad. Afterwards an adult should check whether you need to see a doctor.
100885.m: I cool a sprained foot and raise it.

100886.q: Why do you never put ice directly on the skin?
100886.e: Ice directly on the skin can cause cold damage. That is why you always wrap it in a cloth.
100886.m: I always wrap ice in a cloth.

100887.q: What do you wrap an ice pack in before putting it on the skin?
100887.e: A thin cloth protects the skin from too much cold. The ice pack still cools well.
100887.m: I only put an ice pack on the skin with a cloth.

100888.q: What can you cool with if there is no ice pack?
100888.e: A cloth with cold water also cools. You make it wet again when it gets warm.
100888.m: A wet, cold cloth also cools well.

100889.q: What does cooling often help with?
100889.e: Cooling helps a bump to swell less. If there is a bad headache or vomiting, you must go to the doctor.

100890.q: What happens when you cool a bruise?
100890.e: Cold makes the blood vessels narrower. Less blood leaks out, so the area swells less.

100891.q: What do you cool a small burn with?
100891.e: Cool but not ice-cold water eases the pain. Ice cubes directly on the skin can do harm.
100891.m: I cool a small burn with water.

100892.q: What do you take out of the freezer when you need to cool something quickly?
100892.e: An ice pack is ready in the freezer. You put it, protected, on the injured area.
100892.m: An ice pack from the freezer helps with bumps.

100893.q: Where do ticks wait for people and animals?
100893.e: Ticks sit on grasses and shrubs. They get brushed off onto you as you walk past.
100893.m: Ticks wait in grass and bushes.

100894.q: What do you do after a trip to the woods?
100894.e: Ticks are small and often bite in warm places. If you check yourself, you find them early.
100894.m: After the woods, I check my body for ticks.

100895.q: What is the best way to remove a tick?
a: With tick tweezers or ordinary tweezers
100895.e: With tick tweezers or ordinary tweezers, you grip the tick close to the skin. Then you pull it out slowly.
100895.m: I pull a tick out with tweezers.

100896.q: When are ticks mainly active in Switzerland?
100896.e: Ticks are active when it is warm enough. That is usually from spring into autumn.
100896.m: Ticks are active from spring to autumn.

100897.q: How many legs does an adult tick have?
100897.e: Adult ticks have four pairs of legs. That makes eight legs.
100897.m: Like spiders, ticks have eight legs.

100898.q: What is best to wear in the woods to protect against ticks?
100898.e: Long trousers and closed shoes protect the skin. Then it is harder for ticks to reach your legs.
100898.m: In the woods, I wear long trousers.

100899.q: How long should you keep an eye on the spot after a tick bite?
100899.e: Illnesses after a tick bite sometimes only show up later. That is why you check the spot for a few weeks.
100899.m: After a tick bite, I watch the spot for a few weeks.

100900.q: What is a warning sign a few days after a tick bite?
a: A red ring that gets bigger
100900.e: A red ring that grows is called a bull's-eye rash. Then you must see a doctor, because it can be an illness.
100900.m: If a red ring is growing, I go to the doctor.

100901.q: What does a tick feed on?
100901.e: Ticks bite people and animals and suck blood. They become much fatter as they do so.

100902.q: What often stays stuck in the skin after a bee sting?
100902.e: A honeybee's sting has tiny barbs. That is why it often stays in the skin along with the venom sac.
100902.m: After a bee sting, the sting is often stuck in the skin.

100903.q: How do you remove a bee sting?
a: Do not remove it at all
100903.e: The most important thing is to remove the sting quickly. It is best to scrape it off sideways with a fingernail.
100903.m: I remove a bee sting quickly.

100904.e: Bees only sting when they feel that they or their colony are under threat. The sting is how they defend themselves.
100904.m: A bee stings when it defends itself.

100905.q: When is a sting in the mouth dangerous?
100905.e: A sting in the mouth or throat can swell so much that it is hard to breathe. Then you dial 144 at once and let the person suck ice.
100905.m: If someone is stung in the mouth, I call 144 at once.

100906.q: What is important if someone has a bee allergy?
100906.e: With an allergy, the whole body can react, for example with difficulty breathing. Then you call the emergency number 144 at once.
100906.m: With an allergy, I get help immediately.

100907.q: How should you behave when a bee is flying around you?
100907.e: Hectic movements make bees nervous. People who stay calm get stung less often.

100908.q: Why should you not drink from open cans of fizzy drink outdoors?
100908.e: Wasps like sweet things and crawl into cans. A sting in the mouth is dangerous, so it is better to drink from a glass or with a straw.
100908.m: Outdoors, I look into my glass before drinking.

100909.q: Which insect usually loses its sting when it stings?
100909.e: The honeybee's sting has barbs and gets stuck. Wasps can pull their sting back out.
100909.m: Only the honeybee usually loses its sting when it stings.

100910.q: Roughly how long should you cool a small burn?
100910.e: Cooling for this long eases the pain and protects the skin. For large burns, you call for help immediately.
100910.m: I cool a burn with water for several minutes.

100911.q: What does NOT belong on a burn?
100911.e: Butter, flour or toothpaste make the wound dirty. They can cause an infection.

100912.q: What do you do with a burn blister?
100912.e: The blister protects the skin underneath from germs. That is why you do not pop it.
100912.m: I do not pop a burn blister.

100913.q: What can you easily burn yourself on in the kitchen?
100913.e: Hobs, pans and the oven get very hot. That is why care is important in the kitchen.
100913.m: I am very careful near the hot cooker.

100914.q: What do you do if a person's clothes are on fire?
a: Get them to roll on the ground and get help
100914.e: Running fans the fire. Rolling on the ground or using a fire blanket smothers the flames, and you call for help at once.
100914.m: Burning clothes are smothered on the ground.

100915.e: Hot liquids or steam injure the skin. This is called a scald.
100915.m: Hot water can scald your skin.

100916.q: What can you cool when you have sunburn?
100916.e: Sunburn is a mild burn of the skin. Cool compresses help against the burning feeling.
100916.m: I cool sunburn with damp cloths.

100917.q: When must you call the emergency number at once for a burn?
100917.e: Large burns are dangerous, especially for children. Then you call 144 at once.

100918.q: What do you do first as a child when there is an accident?
100918.e: Adults are better able to help and can call the emergency number. That is why you fetch someone at once.
100918.m: If there is an accident, I fetch an adult at once.

100919.q: What do you pay attention to before helping at the scene of an accident?
100919.e: If you put yourself in danger, you cannot help anyone. The road, for example, is dangerous.
100919.m: When helping, I look after myself first.

100920.q: Who can you ask for help in the playground?
100920.e: Teachers are on playground duty and know what to do. They can also call for help.
100920.m: In the playground, I fetch the teacher.

100921.q: What do you do while an adult calls the emergency number?
100921.e: An injured person is often frightened. If someone stays with them and talks to them, it calms them down.
100921.m: I stay with injured people and comfort them.

100922.q: What can you say to an injured person?
100922.e: Calming words make people feel safer. The person then knows that someone will come soon.
100922.m: I calm injured people with kind words.

100923.q: What do you do if there is no adult nearby?
100923.e: Children may and should call the emergency number too. The control centre will tell you exactly what you can do.
100923.m: Even as a child, I may call the emergency number.

100924.q: How do you call loudly for help?
100924.e: Other people hear loud, clear shouting more quickly. Then they come to help.
100924.m: I call for help loudly and clearly.

100925.q: Which address should you know by heart for emergencies?
a: The address of the zoo in Paris
The address of a toy shop
100925.e: When you make an emergency call, you must say where you are. If you know your address, you can quickly get help to your home.
100925.m: I know my address by heart.

100926.q: What do you tell an adult that you fetch to help?
100926.e: The adult must quickly know what is going on and where to go. That way they can help straight away.
100926.m: I say briefly what has happened and where.

100927.q: What is the phone number of Rega?
100927.e: Rega, the Swiss Air Rescue service, can be reached on 1414.

100928.q: How does Rega usually reach injured people?
